tools.name: memory_status
tools.description: Check what this session is bound to: store, tenant, principal, project and the current history id. Call it first in a session, or when a call fails with history_changed, before retrying anything. Read-only; it never authorizes a model request.

project.description: Project id. Defaults to this session's project.

tools.name: memory_capture
tools.description: Remember something you observed: an error, a test result, a decision, a fact with its source. Give a stable `key` and `request.source_event` for the same event so a retry replays instead of duplicating; the same key with different text is a conflict. Text is stored as untrusted evidence, not as an instruction.

key.description: Retry key: repeat it to replay the first result instead of repeating the write. Minted when omitted.

project.description: Project id. Defaults to this session's project.

source.description: Where it came from, such as pytest or git.

source_event.description: Stable id of the event, so a retry replays.

readers.description: Principals allowed to read it; null means everyone in the project.

observed_at_ms.description: When you observed it, in Unix milliseconds.

supersedes.description: Id of an earlier memory you can read that this replaces.

tools.name: memory_handoff
tools.description: Pass a task to another principal with their current permissions: `prepare` a handoff from a checkpoint, `preview` what the recipient would receive, `materialize` it as the recipient, `ack` or `cancel`. A handoff never widens access; what the recipient cannot see is left out and reported.

tools.name: memory_brief
tools.description: Ask for a briefing before starting work: `brief` with a short query returns mandatory constraints, ranked guidance with sources and a receipt. Read `status` and `reason` first: `blocked` or `budget_insufficient` means decide, not truncate. `rerun` repeats an earlier receipt with a new query. Project, bindings, budget and tokenizer default to the session's.

incarnation.description: History id. Defaults to this session's.
History id. Defaults to this session's.

action.description: Run an earlier briefing again with a new query.

project.description: Project id. Defaults to this session's project.

query.description: What you are about to work on, as a short phrase.

bindings.description: Where this session works (environment, role, path ...). Defaults to the session's.

max_output_tokens.description: Token budget for the reply. Defaults to 6000.

tokenizer.description: Tokenizer used to count the budget. Defaults to the installed one.

top_k.description: At most this many items. Default: 8 for the structured packet; for format text, as many distinct items as fit max_output_tokens, up to 32.

min_score_ppm.description: Leave out guidance whose lexical score (millionths, see each item's lexical_score_ppm) is below this. Default 0: nothing is left out for a low score.

offset.description: Skip this many of the ranked items, to read the next page of the same list (the order is the same for every offset of one query). Default 0.

match.description: all: only records that hold every word of the query (and none if no record does). Default any: ranked by how many of the words, and how well, a record holds.

file.description: Only observations that name this file, symbol or ticket exactly (an anchor found when the record was captured).

run.description: Run id within the task, or null.

valid_ms.description: Judge validity at this Unix-millisecond time.

recorded_position.description: Answer as of this recorded history position.

consistency.description: Whether to wait for recent writes before answering.

freshness.description: How recent the indexed data must be.

dense.description: Whether to use meaning-based search when it is available.

format.description: json (default) returns the structured packet; text returns a cited Markdown rendering in a compact envelope with the same receipt.

as_of_ms.description: Brief as the project stood at this Unix-millisecond time; omit for now.

salience.description: Let your own recent use of memories nudge the ranking.

rerank.description: Let the local cross-encoder reorder the top candidates.

time_range.description: Only records observed in this range (Unix ms, both ends inclusive, either may be left out) are searched; a claim counts when its validity interval overlaps it. Without it, dates in the query only raise matching records in the ranking.

project.description: Project id. Defaults to this session's project.

predecessor.description: Receipt id of the earlier briefing this one follows.

brief.description: The briefing request to run again with a new query.

tools.name: memory_checkpoint
tools.description: Save progress before you stop or hand over: objective, current state, next actions, failed attempts, blockers and verification gaps, under a project, task and expected revision. Use the exact revision you last saw; a conflict means someone else saved first, so resume and merge rather than overwrite.

key.description: Retry key: repeat it to replay the first result instead of repeating the write. Minted when omitted.

run.description: Run id within the task, or null.

expected_revision.description: The revision last seen; null accepts the current revision without a compare-and-set check.

readers.description: Who may read the checkpoint; null keeps the stream's current readers (the writer alone on a first save).

checkpoint.description: The progress to save: objective and current_state are required, the rest optional.

tools.name: memory_plan
tools.description: Track a multi-step plan on a task: `plan_save` creates or revises the whole plan (phases, steps with stable ids, prerequisites), `plan_step` updates one step's status, notes and evidence, `plan_get` reads the current or an earlier revision with computed progress, `plan_list` pages the project's plans. A step counts as done only with evidence; a changed definition needs fresh evidence. Progress is recorded work, not independent certification.
